#981. BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount

BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.

Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW said.

The main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China. Although the company sold more cars in the US and Europe compared to the same period last year, this could only partially offset the decline in China.

BMW's car deliveries in China, which were already at their lowest level since 2017 last year, fell 24.8% in the quarter and consequently dragged global deliveries down by 6.3.

CEO Milan Nedeljkovic said his company would "specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

BMW on Tuesday also lowered its outlook for the current year, citing the faster-than-planned implementation of restructuring measures that includes 8,000 layoffs in its home market.

German carmakers have been struggling to compete with their Chinese counterparts in the electric vehicle market,  resulting in cost-cutting measures.

Volkswagen, the world's second-largest carmaker, is battling mounting competition from falling demand in its core Chinese market.

BMW, and its industry heavyweight peers, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, have announced plans to scale back production and reduce costs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The Volkswagen Group posted its worst quarterly results in more than a decade earlier this October.

It is looking to cut about 15% of its workforce worldwide, or 100,000 jobs, by the end of the decade. BMW has announced that it will cut up to 8,000 jobs — about 5% of its workforce — by the end of 2027.

On the other hand, German auto parts supplier Schaeffler announced on Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe, by 2028.

According to the company statement, three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany.

German automotive supplier Bosch, the world's biggest, announced last year that it would cut 13,000 jobs, mostly in its auto division.

#980. Gyokeres the creator and executioner to see nervous Arsenal past Slavia Prague

With a stylish assist and a gorgeous goal, Viktor Gyokeres produced the sort of match-winning performance that suggests the Swedish striker is making significant progress at last. It has not always been straightforward for him at Arsenal, but this was unquestionably one of his better showings, and it continued an encouraging upturn in his form.

Gyokeres has been the second-choice striker for most of this season, with Mikel Arteta usually preferring the more subtle Kai Havertz in attack. There are signs, though, that Gyokeres is now growing in belief. Following this victory over Slavia Prague, which was much more narrow and nervy than it should have been, he has now scored two goals and registered three assists in his last five appearances.

Even more promising than those statistics was his all-round play in Prague. In the first half especially, Gyokeres held on to long passes, combined with his team-mates and tested the opposition with his runs in behind. For Arsenal’s first goal, he found Noni Madueke with a brilliant pass. For their second, he curled a fabulous strike into the top corner.

“Really good,” said Arteta of Gyokeres. “Not only the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s great news, because I think he needed that performance.”

Those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing. So smooth at first, Arsenal became remarkably ragged by the end. Slavia were deserving of their goal, scored by Wiktor Nowak. It looked like complacency had infected the minds of the Arsenal players, and you could feel Arteta’s fury radiating from the touchline.

“We scored two goals and it should have been three, four or five,” said Arteta. “And at half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning of the second half, we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept, and in everything we discussed. So much to improve and I take full responsibility for that.”

Without Gabriel Magalhães and David Raya, who both made dramatic stops on the goal-line, this could have become an ugly night for Arsenal against one of the weaker teams in the Champions League. The Czech side have now gone 23 games without a victory in Europe’s premier competition, which equals the longest winless run in European Cup history.

It was a remarkable coincidence that this game fell on November 4, the exact date as the same fixture last season. On that occasion Arsenal were comfortable 3-0 winners, with Mikel Merino scoring twice, and they seemed to be heading towards a similar night when Madueke scored the early opener.

The goal was made by Gyokeres, who held off a defender and then hooked an excellent pass into Madueke’s path. The Arsenal winger had already established his dominance over Oskar Kubiak, his opposite number, and he reached fifth gear before the Polish defender had even reached second. Madueke then slid his finish beneath the body of Nazar Domchak, Slavia’s teenage goalkeeper.

A fantastic pass from Gyökeres and a lovely finish from Madueke 🪄 The Arsenal attackers combine to great effect 🤝 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/blmMILZxok

Just as Gyokeres is finding his form, so is Madueke. The absence of the injured Bukayo Saka has given Madueke a run in the side and he seems to be benefiting from it, even if he still lacks the same consistency in decision-making as his England team-mate.

One of Slavia’s many problems in a one-sided first half was their inability to cope with Arsenal’s rotations in midfield. Declan Rice, Martín Zubimendi and Merino were all alternating positions at will, taking turns to drop deep and push forward. Merino could have scored a couple, before he combined sharply with Gyokeres for Arsenal’s second.

Gyokeres has never been the most delicate link-up player, and there have been too many times when the ball has simply bounced off him, but here he was impressively sleek. A quick exchange of passes with Merino allowed him a sight of goal, and the curled finish was sumptuous. For a man known for his power, this was an uncharacteristic demonstration of finesse.

Game over? Arsenal clearly thought so. They certainly came out for the second half like a team that believed the job was done. Arteta became increasingly irate in the first few minutes after the restart, with Ben White on the receiving end of one verbal slap. Rice also received a telling-off, and a yellow card, from the referee after kicking the ball away in annoyance.

Would Slavia have secured a draw if they had been at full strength? They had been weakened by the banishment of their star striker from the club because of a series of disciplinary failings. Tomás Chory, the top scorer for the past two seasons, was chucked out of the team after showing his middle finger to the referee in a recent game. This sort of sanction would have earned Arteta’s approval, no doubt, but it did not increase Slavia’s chances of hurting the Premier League champions in those edgy final few minutes.

Perhaps they will reflect on that decision differently now, given the uncharacteristically wobbly second-half performance by Arsenal. The visitors were vulnerable in the latter stages, when they lacked the control and composure that Arteta expects. Gabriel, too, appeared dismayed by what he was seeing. At one point, he put his hands on his hips and scowled at his team-mates like an angry teacher.

With only a few minutes remaining, Nowak converted a left-wing cross to plunge Arsenal into a proper panic. It required a backs-to-the-wall defensive action, similar to the victory against Liverpool on Sunday, to get over the line.

#977. Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return

Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated."

It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward."

Shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns. In last Friday's ruling, the CAS said that the IIHF's concerns were "not supported by sufficient evidence."

Wednesday's statement comes after two days of talks by the IIHF Council aimed at charting a way forward following Friday's CAS decision, which appears to have caught most of the international ice hockey community off guard.

Two of the organizing committees the statement refers to are those of Canada, which is due to host the IIHF World Junior Championship starting next month, and Germany, which is to host the IIHF Men's World Championship next May. Both countries are strong supporters of Ukraine in its war against Russia, and both have expressed serious reservations about their upcoming tournaments in light of the CAS ruling.

On Tuesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ruled out allowing Russians to compete in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he told reporters at a press conference in Antigua, where he was attending a Commonwealth meeting.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there."

Last weekend, Frank Lutz, chairman of the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) conceded in a television interview that following the CAS decision, the DEB would "also have to consider the option of handing back (hosting rights to) this championship."

In a statement to DW on Wednesday, a German government spokesperson reiterated Berlin's position on the matter from the weekend, saying it viewed Friday's CAS ruling "very critically."

The spokesperson also said  the government would "consult with the German Ice Hockey Federation in the near future regarding the potential consequences of this decision, including its impact on the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany."

Meanwhile, the ice hockey association of Finland, the defending men's world champions, has been spearheading an effort to boycott upcoming IIHF tournaments should the Russians be allowed to compete.

"We are currently working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen said in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Czechia have since made similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson said.

This came shortly after Norway said it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

"Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors.

Czechia Ice Hockey Association President Alois Hadamczik confirmed on Tuesday that they too would refrain from playing Russian teams.

Latvia's federation said it “reaffirms its longstanding and firm position" not to play against Russia or its ally Belarus.

Alexander Helwig, chairman of the Austrian Ice Hockey Association told public broadcaster ORF that “as of now, we would certainly not play against Russia."

USA Hockey has yet to comment on the CAS ruling.

At the same time, sponsors of IIHF tournaments are also getting cold feet. Skoda, which has been the main sponsor of the Men's World Championship for more than three decades, told the Associated Press that it would "reassess" its position if Russia takes part.

"We do not support the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision regarding the participation of Russian national teams in IIHF competitions. With Russia's aggression continuing, we believe the Russian national team's return to the world championship is incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld," the Czech carmaker said.

Skoda isn't alone either, Finnish tire manufacturer Nokian had said it would end its backing if Russia took part and Swedish furniture maker AJ Products, whose logo has been seen on the boards and officials' jerseys at World Championships since 1989, said Monday it would ask for its logo not to be shown.

On Wednesday afternoon, yet another sponsor joined the list, with German workwear company Strauss saying it would "forgo all logo exposure associated with the (men's) tournament" and was considering withdrawing its sponsporship entirely.

With the IIHF Council having failed to agree on how to proceed during its meetings on Monday and Tuesday, President Franz Reindl told Germany's SID news agency on Wednesday, that it would reconvene for further talks on Thursday.

This article was originally published on November 4, 2026. It was updated on November 5, 2026 with the German government statement to DW.

#976. Jack Grealish plays for Everton for the first time since being axed for skipping training without permission in 'breach of club discipline' - as winger comes off the bench during loss at Brentford

Published: 14:08 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:56 EST, 23 November 2026

Jack Grealish returned to the Everton squad for the first time since being made unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline, and came off the bench at half-time against Brentford on Monday.

The Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He had not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a 'breach of club discipline' and a lack of fitness thereafter.

He last featured on October 17, over a month ago, but returned to the match day squad to take on Brentford on Monday night – named on the substitutes' bench. He was introduced at half-time for Tyrique George, with the Toffees 2-0 down and down to 10 men after James Tarkowski's red card. They would ultimately lose 4-0.

Manager David Moyes said ahead of the game: 'He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

'We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don't want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn't be.'

Pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: 'He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?'

Jack Grealish (right) returned to Everton action on Monday for the first time since being punished for missing training

He was named on the bench against Brentford, coming on for Tyrique George at half-time

Everton had won their last three games and went into Monday's match sixth in the table. The result, though, was a blow as they dropped to ninth.

Asked what Grealish can offer, Moyes added: 'Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

'But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

'I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.'

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League group stage match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City from Saxony. The hosts started the day in 27th place in the 36-team table after two defeats, both by four goals to one, in away games against Como and Real Madrid. City begin proceedings in 12th after victories over Porto and AEK sandwiching that rip-roaring 4-2 defeat by the champions PSG at the Etihad.

City, who seemed in rude health after seven successive wins at the start of the Premier League campaign despite the guilty verdicts in the Premier League’s case against them for financial cheating, have wobbled since then, losing their last two league games. Marc Guéhi and Gigi Donnarumma are both suffering bouts of poor form, other individual errors continue to plague them and, although they are creating hatfuls of chances, they have been thwarted by a combination of imprecise finishing and the excellence of Zion Suzuki and Bart Verbruggen.

For all their travails on the road – RB Leipzig have also lost at Werder Bremen, Bayer Leverkusen and Bayern Munich – they have won all their home Bundesliga matches as well as a 1-0 victory over PSV in this competition. Their total of 22 league goals is second only to Bayern’s 27 and Antonio Nusa, a Norway team-mate of Erling Haaland, is in sparkling form flitting behind strikers Christopher Nkunku and Romulo. City, whose full-backs, if you can describe the centre-backs and midfielders who play either side of the centre-halves in that way, never look fit for purpose defensively and may well have their work cut out tonight if he drifts wide.

The Red Bull coaching principles, which have treated us to the dross football of Jesse Marsch, Matthias Jaissle and Ralph Hasenhüttl, all about the long pass, the central channel, counter-pressing and second balls, have a new proponent in Martín Demichelis, the forner City and Argentina defender who won the title in 2014 at the Etihad. Three years ago he led River Plate to the title in Argentina, the highlight of a coaching career also spent running Bayern’s U21s, Monterey and Mallorca.

These two have met six times in the last five years, City winning four, most notably the 7-0 thrashing at the Etihad in 2023’s Round of 16, the year they went on to win the Treble. Leipzig’s only victory came at home five years ago in the sixth, redundant group game when City and PSG had already clinched qualification for the knockout stages.

Antoine Semenyo is City’s only absentee; Leipzig will have to do without one-cap Germany midfielder Assan Ouédraogo and former Chelsea striker Marc Guiu.

#973. Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release

In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

On November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour."

The crowds showed just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

Today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

At first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

For years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

But in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an issue Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

In an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

The controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

Others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

The "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

Despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

The eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been announced, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The new trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO says, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the new production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently said she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

Meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

This article was originally written in German.

#972. Brentford 4-0 Everton: David Moyes' record-breaking night ends in misery as James Tarkowski sees red and rampant Bees boost European hopes

Published: 17:31 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 23 November 2026

David Moyes’ record-breaking night as Everton manager could not have been more miserable.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record for most games in the dugout.

But that was about the only positive he could take away from the Gtech Community Stadium, as high-flying Brentford battered ten-man Everton on an evening to forget for the 63-year-old Scotsman.

Daily Mail Sport's Bobby Manzi was at the Gtech Community Stadium on a torrid night for the Toffees...

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again.

They climbed to sixth, leapfrogging Leeds — who have had far more praise lavished on them this season than Keith Andrews’ reliable side.

Brentford are disciplined with plenty of attacking flair, even with frontman and top goalscorer Igor Thiago suspended.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again

The Premier League lacks quality this season, but Brentford are consistent, losing just twice.

This well-oiled Andrews machine must take advantage of the floundering elite, with Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham all struggling, and finally secure Europe.

‘We set out this season looking to be better than last season, and if that happens, we will be flying to different destinations next season,’ Andrews said of their European hopes.’

‘We've got a very competitive squad that strives to get better. If we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place.

‘I enjoyed us,’ he added about the performance. ‘I thought we were very good. We played with real bravery, courage and energy.’

Brentford limited Everton to just three touches in the penalty area in the first half. They grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck and pinned their opponents back.

Jaidon Anthony was superb on the flank, providing two assists. Midfielder Vitaly Janelt capped off a brilliant display with a wonder strike from 25 yards, finding the top corner with his left foot.

It was a surprise to see Kevin Schade benched but this team is so cohesive, with more focus on the unit than any individual stars, that victory was light work for them.

Both of Keane Lewis-Potter’s goals had an element of fortune attached. But teams earn that luck when they manage ten shots in their opponents’ penalty area in just 45 minutes.

Lewis Potter starred at left-back, registering seven shots — the most of any player — and the joint-most touches in the opposition box. He was a menace and integral to every Brentford attack.

James Tarkowski endured a depressing return to his former club when he was shown the first Premier League red card of his career.

It will split opinion, but in this day and age it is a clear red card. Although the Everton defender won the ball, his studs connected with Yehor Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through. The speed and intensity of the tackle endangered his opponent. He had to go.

Referee Craig Pawson brandished a yellow, but a quick trip to the monitor saw it upgraded. Tarkowski ran down the tunnel before Pawson could even get the red card out of his pocket.

The home support enjoyed it, having taunted their former player throughout the first half.

To compound Everton’s misery, the first game of Tarkowski three-match ban is next weekend’s Merseyside derby.

Although Tarkowski won the ball, his studs connected with Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through

A deflated Moyes had few complaints. ‘My feeling at the time was it wasn’t a red because James easily got to the ball before the Brentford player,’ the Everton boss said.

‘But after I saw it again, Tarky's boot is a bit higher than I'd like, so I can understand why the decision went against us.

‘We didn’t play well. Brentford did and credit to them. A bit unfortunate with the goals, it made it look even worse than it was.’

Everton were unbeaten in four games at Brentford before this and their defeat came in the form of the sublime and the ridiculous.

Tarkowski blocked an initial effort from Lewis-Potter for the second goal but the ball fell straight back to him, and Jake O’Brien helped his second attempt past Jordan Pickford. Once again, Everton should have done better and cleared the initial free-kick.

#971. Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat

The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

"After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat said. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a big relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome."

Themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

"I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat said. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed."

Growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," said Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

"I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat said. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

"I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat said. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a big change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships."

As well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat said, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat said.

"So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she said. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself."

That has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

"The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

Should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she said.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride."

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.

#969. Tuchel: Bellingham and I were up and down – now we are in a good place

England head coach Thomas Tuchel described his relationship with Jude Bellingham as being “in a good place” after admitting it had been “a bit up and down”.

Tuchel has two Bellinghams in his latest England squad after calling up Jude’s brother, Jobe, for the first time for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. If they play together, it will be the first time brothers have represented England in the same team since Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago.

This time last year, Tuchel cast doubt over Jude’s place in his team by picking Morgan Rogers over him, having not included the Real Madrid midfielder in an England squad the previous month.

But Jude performed superbly for Tuchel at the World Cup and was England’s best player during the last international camp. Tuchel revealed he has listened to his advice by calling up 21-year-old Jobe.

Asked if his relationship with Jude has developed, Tuchel said: “It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course, but we are in a good place.

“I love to be his coach, he’s a top player, a very influential player and it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable, he would not perform at that level.

“At the moment, you see he’s happy to come into camp, he’s happy with the role he has, he’s fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them [Bellingham brothers] is just the next step. I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach.”

Jobe has captained England’s Under-21s and, as well as U21 head coach Lee Carlsey, Tuchel acknowledged the influence of Jude on the Borussia Dortmund midfielder’s first senior call.

Jude once said that playing with Jobe for England would be “the biggest dream of my life” and that it would mean more to him than any trophies.

Discussing Jude’s influence on Jobe’s selection, Tuchel said: “We spoke about his brother because I was aware it was always his dream and Jude was always like, ‘Watch him, he’s good, he can make it,’ I would say, ‘Yeah we are watching him.’ And we know, of course, from Lee Carsley and we see him with the Under-21s and there is such positive feedback.

“This is also the signal that if you are good in the Under-21s, this is the next step. We had it with Elliot Anderson, we had it with Alex Scott, we have it with Jarell Quansah and it counts. If you play good for England in the Under-19s, 20s, 21s, if you play good for England in tournaments then it means something.”

Tuchel at one point had to correct himself, with a laugh, when he accidentally referred to Jobe as Jube. On the subject of how Jobe reacted to his call-up and the comparisons with his brother that he will inevitably face, Tuchel said: “He has to live with this that everyone will compare them. They look similar, even in their movements, but they are very different players. And let’s see – they are also different characters, at least that’s what I heard.

“He [Jobe] watched training very early in my [reign]. In my first March camp maybe, he came over and watched his brother train. We chatted and we said, ‘Ah, it would be nice if one day you are with him [Jude].’ He was very kind and polite and I’m glad to have him in camp.

“He couldn’t stop smiling [when I told him]. He has the same beautiful smile as Jude, so it’s nice to have him. Let’s see what the effect is. What I saw, Jude was always the big brother that you imagine, taking care of his younger brother and making sure everything is alright. Behaving like a big brother. And that helps Jobe now. And it will be beautiful for Jude to have his brother close and in camp and to have this experience together. It’s a very special moment for them.”

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of the announcement by Thomas Tuchel of England’s squad for their remaining two Uefa Nations Group 3 matches against Croatia – them again – at Wembley next Thursday and Spain at the Metropolitano in Madrid next Sunday night. England have already qualified for the knockout phase – barring a defeat by Croatia by a margin of eight or more goals – but would need two victories to avoid France and Portugal in the next two-legged phase in March.

Tuchel’s only major injury doubt from the last squad are Arsenal’s Bukao Saka and Como’s Trevoh Chalobah as well as the more long-term absentee Tino Livramento, the man Chalobah replaced in the World Cup 26. Djed Spence has returned to full fitness and played for Inter in their Milan derby defeat last weekend while the head coach’s favourite player, Jordan Henderson, has been passed fit to play for Chelsea at his boyhood club Sunderland on Sunday though at 36 his race may finally have been run at this level despite his unexpected encore in the last 18 months.

For the first time since 2001 England will have the Ballon d’Or winner in the squad and Harry Kane will also become England’s most-capped player – barring some misfortune when Bayern Munich take on Mainz on Saturday – by leading them out at Wembley on Thursday night for his 126th appearance.

Whether he will be joined by Cole Palmer in the squad remains the only significant issue of note. The Chelsea forward pulled out of the last squad as part of his club’s management of his groin injury but he has played in their last four Premier League games, scoring once and being sent off once as well. Kobbie Mainoo is fit again and may be picked to see if his backside has recovered from bench splinters since his summer of exasperation.

The squad will be released at 10am and followed by Tuchel’s explanations, which we will also cover here, an hour later.

In the Fig. 3b legend, in the text now reading “vaccine days 3, 6, 21,” 21 replaces the original “17,” and in the Fig. 3k legend, now reading “vaccine days 3, 6, 20,” 20 replaces the original “21.” In the first sentence of the Methods “Cox proportional hazards regression” section, in the text now reading “For Cox proportional hazards regression, exposures defined relative to an index date...,” “exposures defined relative to an index date” replaces the original “time-dependent variables were defined.” In the first paragraph of the Methods and in the Reporting Summary, data collection timelines have been updated to say “The data-collection cut-off was 1 September 2024 for the NSCLC and melanoma datasets and 1 January 2025 for the tissue agnostic dataset.” Finally, the Acknowledgements have been amended to include the statement that G.A. and N.C. were supported by the CPRIT Research Training Award CPRIT Training Program (RP210028). #967. Aston Villa's Champions League clash with Galatasaray plunged into chaos as Turkish police hunt for a fugitive LION spotted 10 miles from the stadium

Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

Around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

Extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office said in a statement.

A lion has been spotted 10 miles from where Aston Villa are set to play in the Champions League on Tuesday

The Istanbul Governor's Office said 'every effort' is being made to capture the lion alive

Reaction to the lion's escape bordered on the surreal, with one outlet interviewing a person in a lion suit, wearing a Galatasaray shirt, about it. Galatasaray are nicknamed the Lions while Villa have a lion on their badge.

Gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'

Daily Mail Sport has contacted UEFA for an update.

There were even suggestions in Turkey that Villa had cancelled their training session at RAMS Park because of the lion, but Villa did their preparation at Bodymoor Heath for a very different reason – the state of the RAMS Park pitch.

European football chiefs are confident the playing surface will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries. 'We have to think that if there was a risk of injury, we wouldn't be playing on it,' he said. 'The pitch will be better or worse, for both teams.'

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: 'We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.'

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: 'It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.'

Villa, who have been followed abroad by Prince William this season, will take on Galatasaray

Aston Villa shocked Europe by marching straight into the last 16 in the Champions League two seasons ago but a win over Galatasaray will put them on course to repeat it.

Unai Emery’s side have nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase and victory in Istanbul will give them one foot in the knockout rounds.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what Villa can expect from one of the toughest tests on the European calendar.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections of the playing surface at RAMS Park.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen said: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: ‘It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.’

Villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

Repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom)

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

When the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

What next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

Born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

Yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

To invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

There were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet quickly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

Elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

#966. What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one issue ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

Markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

With Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already said he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, said in a note.

"I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind."

Some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

Kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, said the vote showed the extent of that opposition.  Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of big tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

"This election shows that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he said. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted."

If the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown said, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

That sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

"Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office."

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

Trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard said, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump said in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election issue — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

"You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard said. "From a political point of view, that's the most important thing now."

George Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he said in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and issues.

Yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another issue vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the new Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic issues to secure his political survival.

"Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard said. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs."

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

#964. Jayden Bogle receives threats and racist abuse after Leeds’ win over Tottenham

Leeds and the Premier League are launching an investigation into racist abuse and threats sent to Jayden Bogle’s family.

Bogle escaped a red card in the win over Tottenham after injuring Mathys Tel, with the Leeds full-back receiving the threats via social media.

Should Jason Bogle have seen red for this challenge? 🟥👀 📺 Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/fuK42Okkcz

His club have revealed they are looking to identify those who sent messages to the 26-year-old, whose family were threatened in one of the posts seen by Telegraph Sport after the 1-0 victory.

Leeds say they are “appalled at the disgusting, racist social-media abuse Jayden Bogle suffered” and will push for punishments to be taken.

The club added in a statement: “Leeds United condemns this behaviour in the strongest possible terms. There is no place for racism in football or society.

“The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them.

“Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his team-mates, and we all stand with him at this time. Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse.”

Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, described Bogle as the “softest player” in the Premier League who would never try to hurt an opponent.

Referee John Brooks did not issue a yellow card, with VAR Tony Harrington sticking with the on-field decision.

“I’m confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge,” Harrington was quoted on the big screen at Elland Road.

Tottenham will make a formal complaint to Pro Ref over the decision not to send off Bogle.

“I haven’t watched the scenes back so I can’t give you a clear opinion, out of the game it looked a handball but the scene with Jayden was not too far away from my bench and it looked a very unlucky coming together,” Farke said.

“Fingers crossed for Mathys that he is back soon, but it looked like there was not much speed in this action, but Jayden Bogle is one of the most fair players in the country, he would never injure or foul a player on purpose because he is such a fair character.”

Tottenham Hotspur’s purple patch of form ended with a worrying loss. Wearing their “Spurple” kit for the first time, Roberto De Zerbi highlighted a lack of character and personality from his players and refused to blame the defeat on referee John Brooks’s decision not to dismiss Jayden Bogle for leaving one of his players injured.

Spurs’ away strip is based on a 1990s design, but this performance was more Christian Gross than Jürgen Klinsmann or David Ginola. Leeds United created the better chances and eventually broke through with 11 minutes remaining when their substitutes combined for Noah Okafor to score the winning goal.

Noah Okafor came off the bench and broke the deadlock just minutes later ⛓️‍💥 What a finish 🎯 📺 Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/pnbTQM1YpM

After victories against Coventry City, Chelsea and Crystal Palace, this was a blow for De Zerbi after looking to move Spurs into the European places. Leeds had not scored in 298 minutes of football, nor had they won in five previous matches, yet the Tottenham manager could barely recognise the players who had won three matches in a row.

De Zerbi had warned his team they would face a hostile atmosphere at Elland Road, but instead of rising to the challenge, Spurs were passive until it was too late.

“We didn’t win any duels, we didn’t win any one-to-ones, there was space to play and we didn’t take the right position,” De Zerbi said. “We didn’t show personality, we didn’t show what we are or who we are. It is part of the journey for sure. It can be normal in football but we have to be honest, if you are not honest the future is not good. If you analyse our behaviour we can become a top team.

“We worked very hard this week. We spoke all the days about the intensity, the type of game we would have found in this stadium and the atmosphere, it was not a surprise for us. Sometimes it can happen that we didn’t play the kind of game we want.”

De Zerbi’s honesty shines a light on the amount of work that still needs to be done at Spurs. Even after three straight wins, he has refused to get carried away despite fans looking upwards towards the European places.

Neither did the Italian want to blame the officials for failing to send off Bogle. Brooks has history with Spurs, sending off Xavi Simons against Liverpool last season. Here, he booked De Zerbi for his protests after Bogle’s heavy challenge that forced Mathys Tel off through injury.

Bogle trod on his opponent’s foot before clattering into his knee, forcing the French forward off a few minutes later. “I know that Jayden doesn’t foul out of bad intentions, he is not a nasty player and is one of the softest players in the whole league,” Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said. “I call him my butterfly.”

De Zerbi admitted the injury was “bad” and that Tel would now be scanned to determine the extent of the problem. The Spurs boss was upset that Pedro Porro was later booked for a similar challenge, while Bogle went unpunished – but he said the referee was not the cause of the defeat.

“I was surprised because in the same position in the second half there were two different fouls, the yellow card for Pedro Porro is not possible. I don’t know if it is a red card or not on Mathys Tel but the parameter of the referee was not good enough for this in both situations,” De Zerbi said.

Okafor was only on the pitch for 97 seconds before he finished off a move made by Farke’s replacements. Half-time substitute Melvin Bard sent a throw-in to Harry Wilson, who had also just come on and Okafor did the rest, bursting past Rodrigo Bentancur and planting his finish into the bottom corner. It meant the home fans were singing their “I Predict A Riot” winning anthem for just the second time this season.

For Leeds, moving into the top half will lift their own hopes of challenging for Europe, such is the congested mid-table.

“For us it has been a difficult period, we are missing key players like Anton Stach, Noah, Dominic [Calvert-Lewin] has not had the easiest spell with several injury problems and it was important to show this unity and commitment to avoid all their individual quality to score goals and reduce them to very little,” Farke added.

“Our final third, the quality was perhaps not there but second half there was no doubt just one team was pushing for that win. Another clean sheet another terrific defensive behaviour.”

Archie Gray will make his first appearance against his old club today after joining Spurs from Leeds in 2024. He was an unused sub in the two matches last season but is now an established part of this De Zerbi resurgence, starting all but two matches in the current campaign. Gray was named in the England Under-21 squad yesterday but is heading in the right direction for a senior call-up.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is starting for Leeds today, after doubts over a foot issue heading into the Elland Road fixture. He was named in the England squad yesterday, which suggested he was not ruled out of this clash against Spurs

Roberto De Zerbi has kept a settled team as he looks to make it four Premier League wins in a row. Dominic Solanke is dropped to the bench in his only change, with Pedro Porro coming in – so it may be Omar Marmoush playing as a central forward.

There are many processes in [Tottenham’s] build-up. You need players to interpret this and the legs to cover the centre of the game. It is always complicated [tactically against a De Zerbi team], very dominant in possession. You have to find solutions to be competitive in this area.

The most important thing is what happens on the pitch but [we have bought] Sean [in because of the] tactical aspect. He is sop smart, has experience and also the legs to compete. It’s necessary to have a third midfielder on the pitch to control their processes. On the other hand he is sharp on the offensive actions, many times. Lukas [Nmecha] brings the greediness, physicality and can take the attention off Dominic. he has been very sharp in training, scoring many goals and for that he has the chance to shine today.

Dominic is a key player and thank God he was able to join us in team training yesterday. Overall he is in a good position.

You will always have spells in the Premier League when you cannot convert good performances into results or when you can’t score many goals. We are struggling with injuries for key players in our attack – Noah Okafor, Anton Stach – but hopefully we have also turned the corner.

The pre-season, it was clear [he is] a special talent. You recognise the special talent immediately and he doesn’t need to show something special, you understand? Everything that he does and he is one of the special talents.

The next step he has to enjoy, he has to follow the older players, the players with more experience like [Andrew] Robertson, [James] Maddison, Ben Davies and to find the time to play.

It is my responsibility because when you manage young players and sucho big talents like Luca, it is a bigger responsibility for me.

He has to be ready when he goes on the pitch. I think it [does] not depend on the result, he can play from the beginning. Before the Chelsea game, I thought to play with him in the first XI, but in the end you have to find the right moment and for them also.

I think the age is not so important. The most important is the quality, personality, the behaviour on the pitch and the qualities. And Luca has all of these qualities.

Leeds United are heartbroken to learn of the passing of supporter Colin Westby at the age of 68. Colin suffered a medical emergency ahead of our Premier League fixture with Manchester United on Sunday 18 October at Elland Road. After being transferred to hospital, he was placed into a medically induced coma and sadly following a period of unresponsiveness, the decision was made to withdraw life support. Colin was a long-standing Season Ticket Holder at the club, attending matches for over 50 years. The thoughts of everyone at Leeds United are with Colin's family and friends at this sad time. We will pay tribute to Colin in the 68th minute of our next Premier League fixture with Tottenham Hotspur, on Saturday 7 November.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. The home side, lions at night and mice in the morning, have the unenviable record of 21 top-flight matches with a kick-off time before 3pm without a win. All that extra TV moolah comes in handy but their home ground, a bearpit under the floodlights, is neutered when its denizens are yawning instead of being fired up by social lubricant.

Daniel Farke’s team started the campaign well but are now without a win in five, drawing three matches with teams beneath them in the table – Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Sunderland – and  losing to two above them, Arsenal and Bournemouth. In fairness they played well against the champions for an hour and were deservedly in the lead until Mikel Arteta turnd to his billionaire’s bench and changed the game. At Bournemouth last week they also made a decent start, had a goal disallowed for striking Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s arm and then James Trafford chucked one in.

They never recovered, found themselves increasingly bogged down when trying to unlock a low block and were mugged on the break in added time to lose 2-0. They are a robust side overly reliant on their wing-backs to create chances for their No 9 in the absence of the injured Noah Okafor who was unavailable to train with the team this week because of a groin injury but may be fit enough for the bench.

Spurs, by contrast, are buoyant following three wins on the bounce – over Coventry, Chelsea and Palace, two with clean sheets – that has taken them from 19th to ninth, three places above Leeds. They have won their last three visits to Elland Road, 0-4 under Antonio Conte, which proved to be the last match of Marcelo Bielsa’s glorious spell at the Peacocks, 1-4 under Ryan Mason, which sealed Leeds’ relegation, and 1-2 under Tomas Frank last year by virtue of goals from Mathys Tel and Mohammed Kudus as the home side struggled against their width back in the days before their switch to a back three.

Tel also scored in Spurs’ home game, a 1-1 draw in May, and then kicked Ethan Ampadu in the head to concede the penalty from which Leeds equalised. I wonder what kind of impact he will have today. Incidentally Roberto De Zerbi on his last visit to Leeds when manager of Brighton in 2022-23 had such a strop on the touchline when the home team equalised that he was within a gnat’s whisker of being sent off.

#962. Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football

The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a video on his Instagram account.

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.

The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward represented his country 234 times, scoring 146 goals — making him the men's record-holder for ⁠international ​appearances and for international goals.

He captained Portugal ​to their first major trophy at ​Euro 2016 and led them to the 2019 and 2025 Nations League titles.

"It was not an easy decision, there are decisions that are not ​only with the head. They are also made with the heart," Ronaldo continued in the Instagram post.

"If I ever made you happy, ​if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel ⁠proud ​of our country, then it ​was all worth it."

He also thanked his family, the Portuguese people ​and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his national ​team career.

The Portuguese Football Association (FPF) released a statement expressing its gratitude and respect for the player also known as "CR7."

"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" it read.

The FPF intends to organize a tribute "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much."

While his long-rival Lionel Messi ended his Argentina career with a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance may go down as Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, depending on the nature of the tribute. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus left him on the bench for the following match and said he wouldn't start the next one.

Ronaldo responded by walking out of the Portugal training camp. He was subsequently suspended and fined by the FPF, but he had been expected to return to Portugal for the November international break.

Like Messi, Ronaldo intends to continue his club career with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.
